messages:
mike: FYI support ticket from AcmePay about recurring 504s for their hosted requests, started ~18:20 UTC. p95 spiking to 28s.
eng-oncall-bot: Incident created: #INC-4625 · assigned to eng-oncall · severity P1 · start 4625001234
sara: I pulled a flamegraph and traces. Looks like request queue depth for their tenant is hitting the per-host queue cap and creating a long tail in continuous-batcher.
mike: Any recent deploys?
sara: No deploys in the last 6h. Telemetry shows steady rate from AcmePay + a short burst of very short requests ~18:18 that cause churn.
support_julie: Customer says behavior started after they rolled a client that retries aggressively (backoff=0ms). They sent a few traces / req-ids: req:acme-0a1b2, req:acme-0a1b3.
miguel: Can you paste the sample logs?
support_julie: ```
[18:20:12] gateway: enqueue request tenant=acmepay q_depth=128 q_limit=128 route=/v1/generate req_id=acme-0a1b2
[18:20:12] batcher: started batch size=4 latency_ms=5
[18:20:40] gateway: dequeue request tenant=acmepay q_depth=128 wait_ms=18600 req_id=acme-0a1b2
[18:20:40] proxy: upstream 504 model-host-7 req_id=acme-0a1b2
```
mike: ugh. q_depth==q_limit and wait_ms of 18s. That matches the p95.
lisa: We have per-host queue caps to protect other tenants; seems acmepay saturating their slot and causing dead time for tail requests.
miguel: Two-pronged ask: short-term mitigation to stop customer impact, and long-term fix for aggressive retry patterns that monopolize batching.
sara: Short-term: throttle AcmePay API key to reduce Q occupancy, and enable early-reject for requests with body_size==0 (their clients send tiny requests). Also we can pin them to dedicated capacity if they want no noisy-neighbor risk.
mike: Can we throttle at the gateway quickly? How to do that without a deploy?
miguel: We have runtime rate-limit rules. I can add a tenant rule now: allow 100 rps burst 200 -> 20s window. Will it block existing inflight queue? It will prevent new enqueues.
sara: Also flip on debug tracing for continuous-batcher to capture batch formation timestamps. Set SAMPLE_BATCHER=1 for their tenant.
support_julie: I told AcmePay we are doing a throttling test and asked them to disable the new retry client. They agreed to pause for 15m.
eng-oncall-bot: Action taken: tenant throttle rule applied for tenant=acmepay by miguel at 4625001258 · details: max_rps=100 burst=200
mike: After throttle, telemetry shows q_depth falling from 128 -> 30 over 45s and p95 dropped to 3.2s. :thumbsup:
sara: Repro steps we used for internal debugging: 
1) curl -H "Authorization: Bearer ACME_KEY" -d '{"prompt":"x"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate --repeat 400 --concurrency 10
2) watch gateway metrics: `tenant_queue_depth{tenant="acmepay"}`
3) observe continuous-batcher logs for batch formation timestamps.
miguel: Long-term: add fairness token bucket inside batcher to avoid long-lived tiny-reqs dominating slots and change queue cap to be per-tenant-group instead of per-host. Also consider adding a short-circuit for <50ms client retries to contribute to a retry-score and lower priority.
lisa: Also need a customer-facing postmortem note and recommended client fix: exponential backoff + jitter.
support_julie: AcmePay is happy with the throttle for now and will roll back the aggressive retry. They requested ETA for a platform-side mitigation.
miguel: I'll draft a roadmap ticket: RB#7789 "batcher fairness & retry-aware queueing" ETA 2 weeks.
sara: Add unit tests for priority fairness and a staging perf run to validate tail p95 under synthetic retries.
mike: Nice work. Keep this thread for final postmortem snippets.
eng-oncall-bot: Incident closed: #INC-4625 · resolved 4625001298 · root cause: tenant-saturation-by-aggressive-retries causing continuous-batcher backlog and tail-timeouts
